title: Preprocessing scan bound
statement: Let $x$ and $r$ be finite Boolean strings, let $i$ be a natural number, and let $c$ be a configuration of the zero-work-tape Boolean machine on input $x$. Suppose that removing the first $i$ bits of $x$ gives $r$, that $i\leq |x|$, that $c$ is in state $\mathrm{scan0}$, and that its input head is at position $i+1$. For the machine whose scan state emits each examined bit and, after examining two consecutive unequal bits, starts its rewrite phase, there is a time $t\leq |r|+1$ when it is in state $\mathrm{rwStart}$ and its output is the output already in $c$, followed by the string obtained from $r$ by retaining its first two bits and continuing recursively while each examined pair is equal (retaining a final singleton if present).
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a zero-work-tape configuration on input $x
Removing the first $i$ bits of $x$ gives $r$
caveat: The supplied snippet uses the machine `preTM` but does not include its definition, so its transition behavior cannot be fully verified from the stated ground truth.
